{{Short description|Immigrant holding facility in El Cajon, California, US}}
{{Use American English|date=September 2025}}
[[File:San_Diego_County_California_Incorporated_and_Unincorporated_areas_El_Cajon_Highlighted_0621712.svg|thumb|right|Location of El Cajon in San Diego County]] 
'''Casa San Diego''' is a holding facility located in [[El Cajon, California]], for minors who are either unaccompanied at the [[Borders of the United States|United States border]] or who have been separated from their families. Currently, around 10 percent of children housed in Casa San Diego were separated from their parents on entry at the border.<ref name="Morrissey 2018">{{Cite news|url=http://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/news/immigration/sd-me-family-separation-20180618-story.html|title=When children are separated from their parents at the border, here is where they go next|last=Morrissey|first=Kate|date=18 June 2018|work=San Diego Union Tribune|access-date=2018-06-18|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180618220913/http://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/news/immigration/sd-me-family-separation-20180618-story.html|archive-date=18 June 2018|language=en-US}}</ref> Casa San Diego currently houses boys and girls between the ages of 6 and 17.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.kpbs.org/news/2018/jun/18/nancy-pelosi-other-congress-members-tour-san-diego/|title=Nancy Pelosi, Other Congress Members, Tour San Diego Immigration Detention Facilities|date=18 June 2018|work=KPBS Public Media|access-date=2018-06-18|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180618221602/http://www.kpbs.org/news/2018/jun/18/nancy-pelosi-other-congress-members-tour-san-diego/|archive-date=18 June 2018|language=en}}</ref>

== About ==
The facility of Casa San Diego is run by [[Southwest Key Programs]] and located in [[El Cajon, California]].<ref name="Morrissey 2018" /> It is under 24-hour video surveillance and has an alarm that sounds when unauthorized individuals open the front door.<ref name="Morrissey 2018" /> There are classrooms, a recreation area and a medical clinic.<ref name="Ryan 2018">{{Cite news|url=https://www.thecut.com/2018/06/inside-ursula-border-patrol-center-family-separation.html|title=Inside 3 Detention Centers Where Immigrant Children Are Kept From Their Parents|last=Ryan|first=Lisa|date=18 June 2018|work=The Cut|access-date=2018-06-18|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180618222337/https://www.thecut.com/2018/06/inside-ursula-border-patrol-center-family-separation.html|archive-date=18 June 2018|language=en}}</ref> The entire facility is fenced in with [[privacy netting]].<ref name="Ryan 2018" />

Minors held at the facility remain there for an average 45 days while they wait for the [[United States Department of Health and Human Services|Department of Health and Human Services]] to place them into [[Foster care|foster]] custody, with family members or to be [[Deportation|deported]] to their home country.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://fox5sandiego.com/2018/06/15/touring-the-east-countys-shelter-for-immigrant-children/|title=Touring the East County's shelter for immigrant children|last=Meyer|first=Matthew|date=2018-06-16|work=fox5sandiego.com|access-date=2018-06-18|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180616143939/http://fox5sandiego.com/2018/06/15/touring-the-east-countys-shelter-for-immigrant-children/|archive-date=16 June 2018|language=en-US}}</ref>
